Neural Harmonic Textures (NHT) is a primitive-based neural representation that increases the expressive power of individual primitives by anchoring latent feature vectors to a virtual scaffold surrounding each primitive, applying periodic activations to interpolated features, and decoding the accumulated signal via a single deferred MLP pass [S1].

The claim accurately summarizes the core methodology of Neural Harmonic Textures (NHT) as described in the evidence. Specifically: 1) It is a primitive-based neural representation. 2) It increases expressive power by anchoring latent feature vectors to a virtual scaffold (e.g., tetrahedra vertices) surrounding each primitive. 3) It applies periodic activations (sine and cosine) to interpolated features. 4) It decodes the accumulated signal via a single deferred MLP pass. All these points are explicitly stated in the abstract, introduction, and notes of Source [S1].
supported
